display: English lecturer in Lanzhou (sixth year teaching oral English and academic writing), dog owner, blogs about daily life here.

signals.text: I'm looking for someone in Lanzhou who can bridge Chinese and English at a vet's office, or a vet who can explain things in plain English.
I'm designing a new spring elective, 'English for science writing', and the syllabus is due December 5. I'd like input from people who write or teach scientific papers.
I'd like to travel to Dunhuang in winter, but I don't know yet whether I can go.
My 14-year-old golden retriever has been eating less and breathing heavily at night. Two clinics have given me different impressions.
I have a vet report in Chinese, full of abbreviations and numbers, that a translation app can't make sense of. I don't know which questions to ask.
A vet mentioned something about her heart and raised the question of whether she is suffering. I need a second opinion and someone to help me understand what that means.
I have a vet follow-up on October 5 at 3pm, and I'd like someone to come with me or be on call to interpret.
I teach Monday to Thursday on a fixed schedule, so I can only meet or travel on Fridays, weekends or evenings.
I can spend about 5,000 RMB on vet bills this month and need to know what that realistically covers.
I'm afraid of losing my dog, and I find it hard to talk about. I'd like to talk with someone who has been through the end of a pet's life.
My brother and I disagree about our mother's care home costs, and I'm sending what I can from China. It's a sore subject and I feel guilty.
I feel isolated in Lanzhou. I miss having someone who knows me well, and I've been losing focus in class lately.

offers.text: Six years of university-level teaching in China: oral English, academic writing, and now science writing.
TEFL certificate and an MA in applied linguistics (Ohio State). I can give feedback on English papers, abstracts and presentations.
I can be a native-speaker conversation partner for English practice, especially for students or researchers in Lanzhou.
I know the foreign-teacher community in Gansu, about fifteen people, and can introduce newcomers or share local practical tips.
I run a blog about teaching in Lanzhou with a few hundred readers, and I can write about or promote relevant projects.
I've moved a senior dog internationally twice (Ohio to Chengdu, then Lanzhou). I can share what the process involved for expats with pets.
I live in a small apartment near campus with a dog-friendly landlord, which may help other expats looking for pet-friendly housing leads.
I can swap English help for Chinese help, especially medical or practical vocabulary.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a vet (or vet student) in Lanzhou and I speak English. If you send me your dog's report I can explain it.
catchers.can: Caleb can share the dog's report and questions, and arrange an interpreter or a second consultation.
catchers.confirm: Can you explain cardiac terms and test results in English, rather than just translating word for word?

catchers.hypo: My neighbour is a vet and I can introduce you. Is your dog a senior with heart or breathing problems?
catchers.can: Through Dr. Wang, Caleb already has a lead to a neighbour vet, and he could accept further introductions the same way.
catchers.confirm: Is the vet you're recommending experienced with senior dogs and heart conditions, and willing to see a foreign client with an interpreter?

catchers.hypo: I lost my old dog last year, and I know how hard those decisions are. I'm happy to just talk.
catchers.can: Caleb can listen and talk, and he will also share a few practical things he has learned.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally gone through making an end-of-life decision for a long-time pet?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Cincinnati social worker who helps families compare memory-care and nursing homes. Is anyone looking for options?
catchers.can: Caleb's brother Mark handles his mother's care in Ohio and is looking for cheaper options. Caleb can pass him a referral.
catchers.confirm: Do you advise families on care homes in the Cincinnati area, and could you work with a family member who is abroad and contributing only partially?

catchers.hypo: I'm a master's student in Lanzhou working on my English paper and I'd like someone to read my abstract.
catchers.can: Caleb can review the abstract and give writing feedback.
catchers.confirm: Is your paper in English and in a scientific field, and do you need feedback on style and structure rather than a ghostwriter?

catchers.hypo: I'm a researcher who publishes papers, and I'd like to guest-talk about science writing to a class.
catchers.can: Caleb could invite you to guest-teach or advise on his spring elective.
catchers.confirm: Can you speak or advise in English, specifically about writing and publishing scientific papers?

catchers.hypo: I've travelled to Dunhuang and Jiayuguan in winter with an older dog. Here's what worked.
catchers.can: Caleb could use this to decide whether the trip is feasible, and which parts of the route are safe for her.
catchers.confirm: Did you personally take a senior dog on the Lanzhou-Jiayuguan-Dunhuang route in winter?

catchers.hypo: I'm a foreign teacher who just arrived in Lanzhou and I don't know anyone yet.
catchers.can: Caleb can introduce you to the Gansu foreign-teacher circle and tell you what he wishes he'd known.
catchers.confirm: Are you a foreign teacher or worker living in Gansu rather than just visiting?

forbids.text: I can't leave Lanzhou for long while my dog is unwell.
My Chinese is not good enough to argue or negotiate in medical or technical terms, so I need an interpreter for those.
My teaching schedule is fixed Monday to Thursday, so I can't meet on those days.
My vet budget is limited to about 5,000 RMB this month.

projects.name: English for science writing (spring elective)
projects.text: A new university elective teaching students to write English scientific papers. The syllabus is due December 5.
roles_needed: sample paper and teaching material contributor

projects.name: Dunhuang winter trip
projects.text: A five-day January trip to the Mogao caves, flying Lanzhou to Jiayuguan and then taking the train. It is on hold until his dog's health is clearer.

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share my dog's symptoms, vet visits and my schedule, and my vet report in part if you're a vet.
policy.t2: Once trust is established I'll share how I'm coping, my family tension over my mother's care, and my money limits.
policy.never: My own medical records and any bank details.
